_comment: Source of truth for bug-check (stop) code lookups. The dump parser reads this to translate a numeric stop code into a human-readable name and description. Keyed by the canonical 0x-prefixed 8-digit hex string. This is a curated subset covering codes the test harness produces plus the most common real-world crashes; extend as needed. Do not copy these entries into any script.

0x0000000A.name: IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL
0x0000000A.description: Kernel-mode process or driver accessed memory at an IRQL that was too high. Usually an invalid memory reference by a driver.

0x00000019.name: BAD_POOL_HEADER
0x00000019.description: The pool header for a kernel memory allocation is corrupt. Causes include double frees, buffer overruns into adjacent pool blocks, and use-after-free writes.

0x0000001E.name: KMODE_EXCEPTION_NOT_HANDLED
0x0000001E.description: A kernel-mode program generated an exception the error handler did not catch.

0x00000050.name: PAGE_FAULT_IN_NONPAGED_AREA
0x00000050.description: Referenced invalid system memory. Often faulty hardware (RAM) or a driver accessing freed memory.

0x0000007E.name: SYSTEM_THREAD_EXCEPTION_NOT_HANDLED
0x0000007E.description: A system thread generated an exception the error handler did not catch.

0x0000007F.name: UNEXPECTED_KERNEL_MODE_TRAP
0x0000007F.description: The CPU generated a trap the kernel did not expect. Parameter 1 = 0x8 is a double fault, typically from kernel stack exhaustion (stack overflow).

0x00000080.name: NMI_HARDWARE_FAILURE
0x00000080.description: Hardware malfunction reported via non-maskable interrupt (NMI); also produced by a hardcoded breakpoint trap.

0x0000009F.name: DRIVER_POWER_STATE_FAILURE
0x0000009F.description: A driver is in an inconsistent or invalid power state, typically during a power transition.

0x000000BE.name: ATTEMPTED_WRITE_TO_READONLY_MEMORY
0x000000BE.description: A driver attempted to write to a read-only memory segment (e.g. its own code pages). Parameter 1 is the virtual address written.

0x000000C1.name: SPECIAL_POOL_DETECTED_MEMORY_CORRUPTION
0x000000C1.description: Driver Verifier Special Pool detected memory corruption around a pool allocation. Only raised when Driver Verifier's Special Pool feature is active. Parameter 1 is the address that was being freed or corrupted.

0x000000C2.name: BAD_POOL_CALLER
0x000000C2.description: A thread made a bad pool request, such as freeing the same allocation twice (double free) or freeing an already-freed pool block.

0x000000C9.name: DRIVER_VERIFIER_IOMANAGER_VIOLATION
0x000000C9.description: Driver Verifier's I/O Verification detected a driver violation. Parameter 1 identifies the specific rule broken. Only raised when Driver Verifier is active.

0x000000D1.name: DRIVER_IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL
0x000000D1.description: A driver accessed pageable (or invalid) memory at an IRQL that was too high (DISPATCH_LEVEL or above).

0x000000EF.name: CRITICAL_PROCESS_DIED
0x000000EF.description: A critical system process terminated unexpectedly.

0x000000F7.name: DRIVER_OVERRAN_STACK_BUFFER
0x000000F7.description: A driver overran a stack-based buffer; the GS stack-cookie check detected corruption.

0x0000003B.name: SYSTEM_SERVICE_EXCEPTION
0x0000003B.description: An exception occurred while executing a system service routine, often from corrupted code or memory.

0x00000133.name: DPC_WATCHDOG_VIOLATION
0x00000133.description: The DPC watchdog detected a single long-running DPC or an overall time-limit violation, often a stuck driver.

0x00000139.name: KERNEL_SECURITY_CHECK_FAILURE
0x00000139.description: The kernel detected corruption of a critical data structure (e.g. a stack-buffer overrun caught by /GS or Control Flow Guard). Parameter 1 identifies the check type; 0x2 = stack cookie / stack buffer overrun. On modern Windows this supersedes 0xF7 for driver stack-overrun crashes.

0x0000007B.name: INACCESSIBLE_BOOT_DEVICE
0x0000007B.description: Windows lost access to the system partition during boot, often a storage-controller driver or configuration issue.

0x00000124.name: WHEA_UNCORRECTABLE_ERROR
0x00000124.description: A fatal hardware error reported through the Windows Hardware Error Architecture (WHEA).

0x0000001A.name: MEMORY_MANAGEMENT
0x0000001A.description: The memory manager detected a severe error. Parameter 1 identifies the subtype; 0x3F is a page-hash (CRC) mismatch between the page read from disk and the expected checksum, indicating storage-path data corruption.

0x0000003D.name: INTERRUPT_EXCEPTION_NOT_HANDLED
0x0000003D.description: An exception occurred in an interrupt service routine (ISR) that was not handled. Often caused by register corruption in a driver's ISR path.

0x0000007A.name: KERNEL_DATA_INPAGE_ERROR
0x0000007A.description: A page of kernel data could not be read into memory. Parameter 2 is the NTSTATUS; 0xC0000185 (STATUS_IO_DEVICE_ERROR) points at a storage-path failure. Common in environments with intermittent disk or SAN connectivity.

0x00000109.name: CRITICAL_STRUCTURE_CORRUPTION
0x00000109.description: The kernel detected corruption of a critical system data structure (e.g. a function-pointer table, processor control region, or object-type list). Usually hardware failure or a driver overwriting kernel memory.

0x00000135.name: REGISTRY_FILTER_DRIVER_EXCEPTION
0x00000135.description: A registry filtering driver (e.g. an antivirus minifilter) caused an unhandled exception during a registry callback. Often WdFilter.sys (Defender) on an in-page error.

0x00000154.name: UNEXPECTED_STORE_EXCEPTION
0x00000154.description: A store component caught an unexpected exception, commonly triggered by a failing disk, corrupt page file, or antivirus interference with store operations.

0x00020001.name: HYPERVISOR_ERROR
0x00020001.description: The hypervisor encountered a fatal error. Common causes include unhandled exceptions during hypercalls (e.g. TLB-flush or IPI delivery) and hardware-enforced alignment faults (split-lock #AC) forwarded as fatal NMIs to the guest.
